notice.s1.text: {app} is an open source project maintained by volunteers. For questions or reports you can open a public issue in the project repository: do not write personal data.
notice.s1.title: Who we are
notice.s2.text: Nothing: the spectra and libraries you load are read and processed only in your browser, on your computer. They are not sent to the project or to third parties. The project has no server that would receive them.
notice.s2.title: What we do with your files
notice.s3.text: Your preferences (language, theme), the libraries you have imported and a copy of the site for use without a network. Sample data disappear when you close the page, unless you turn on the local archive: in that case they stay on your computer until you delete them (button “Delete all”) or until the automatic deletion after the number of days set. If the computer is shared, other people may see them.
notice.s3.title: What stays on your computer
notice.s4.text: No cookies, visit statistics, advertising, or third-party fonts or scripts.
notice.s4.title: No tracking
notice.s5.text: The site is hosted by GitHub Pages (GitHub, Inc.). GitHub records the IP address of visitors for security reasons, even without an account; the project has no access to these data.
notice.s5.title: Hosting of the site
notice.s6.text: When you export a file (spectrum, result, contribution), the program removes sample names, paths, users, serial numbers and times, and shows you a preview. It is up to you to decide whether and to whom to send it.
notice.s6.title: Exports
notice.s7.text: If you propose a spectrum to the community library, you publish it yourself through GitHub (the “Community database policy” applies). The name or pseudonym you choose as author will be public.
notice.s7.title: Contributions
notice.s8.text: Since the project does not process the personal data of visitors, there are no data for you to consult, correct or delete with us; for the data processed by GitHub, its privacy statement applies. You can still open a public issue in the project repository, without personal data.
notice.s8.title: Rights

teoria.title: How FTIR works
warnings.s1.text: {app} is a program that supports the qualitative analysis of infrared spectra (FTIR-ATR), designed for staff with chemical training in harm reduction services, teaching and research. It proposes candidates and explains the peaks; the decision on the identity of the sample always belongs to the qualified person who analyses it and signs the result.
warnings.s1.title: What it is
warnings.s2.text: It is not a medical device, it does not diagnose, and it gives no therapeutic advice or doses. It is not an accredited laboratory analysis and has no legal or forensic value.
warnings.s2.title: What it is not
warnings.s3.text: FTIR identifies the main components well; it does not reliably detect components below about 5 % by weight; it does not rule out the presence of active substances at very low doses (for example fentanyl and analogues, which in samples can be at 3-10 % or less, and nitazenes); it does not quantify; isomers and analogues can have very similar spectra. A component that is not found is not a component that is absent.
warnings.s3.title: Limits of the measurement
warnings.s4.text: The result depends on the libraries used (name and version are shown in every result), on the quality of the spectrum and on the settings. A substance that is not in the libraries cannot be recognised: at most the program points out bands that are compatible with a class.
warnings.s4.title: Limits of the libraries
warnings.s5.text: Scores measure the similarity between spectra, not the probability that the sample is that substance. The calculation method is described in the documentation.
warnings.s5.title: Scores
warnings.s6.text: The program will never say “safe”, “pure”, “clean” or “all clear”. No result makes the use of a substance safe.
warnings.s6.title: Words the program does not use
warnings.s7.text: The information on effects, risks and harm reduction in the sheets is reviewed by health staff (reviewer name and date on every sheet); it does not replace a conversation with the workers or the opinion of a doctor. In an emergency: 112.
warnings.s7.title: Health texts
warnings.s8.text: The program is distributed “as is”, without warranty, under the licences MIT OR Apache-2.0; the data under their licences (CC BY 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0 or the terms of the rights holder).
warnings.s8.title: No warranty
warnings.s9.text: The files you load stay in your browser and are not sent to anyone (see “Privacy notice”).
warnings.s9.title: Your data
warnings.short: Result proposed by the program, to be checked and signed by the chemist. FTIR does not see components below about 5 % and does not rule out potent substances at low doses (fentanyl and analogues, nitazenes). It does not say how much there is. A result does not mean that the substance is safe.
